question.text: Will US and Iranian negotiators meet in person in November or December 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, after October 31, 2026 and before January 1, 2027, negotiators from Iran and the United States meet in person, anywhere in the world.
question.fine_print:
"Negotiator" is defined as any official or envoy who has authorization to negotiate on behalf of their government.

"In person" means at least one negotiator on behalf of the US executive branch and at least one negotiator on behalf of Iran's national government occupying the same venue. Interpreters or mediators are permitted, including if they are shuttling between the two sides (thus the meeting need not be face-to-face to count). 

In order to count, the meeting must be reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) as any talks or negotiations on US-Iran issues (such as a ceasefire, Iran's nuclear program, the status of the Strait of Hormuz, or sanctions).

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46314) which opened on 2026-10-26 17:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

# US-Iran in-person negotiations, Nov-Dec 2026: research summary

**In short:** As of Nov 3, I found no report of US and Iranian negotiators meeting in person in November. The talks running now are indirect, through Qatar. A deal draft is circulating and a follow-up meeting has been floated, but no date or venue is set. US strikes after the midterms are being openly discussed. Markets put the chance of a senior meeting by Dec 31 at about 46-47%.

## 1. Resolution source
- No data series decides this. It resolves from credible media reports, via Metaculus question 46314. I found no official list of meetings.
- 2026-11-03: Polymarket's market "Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by Oct 31" shows 0/1, meaning it resolved No. That suggests the late-October Doha contacts did not count as a senior US-Iran meeting.

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. Every report I found from Oct 29 to Nov 3 describes Iranians meeting only Qatari mediators, with Washington coordinating remotely. No source places US negotiators in Doha at the same time.
- Note on the rules: Qatari shuttling counts if both sides are in the same venue (as in New York on Sep 22). An indirect round with both teams in one city would therefore resolve Yes.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Qatar's Foreign Ministry says both sides are reviewing the mediators' proposals and differences remain. A senior Iranian official told Reuters the sides are "far from agreement," and Iran ties any deal to ending the US naval blockade. Gulf allies were reportedly told to prepare for possible US strikes after Nov 4. Iran's Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, reportedly ordered the armed forces to prepare for war. [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202611035924)
- 2026-11-03: Iranian spokesperson Baghaei says there is "no new development." Exchanges through mediators continue. [Gazete Oksijen](https://gazeteoksijen.com/dunya/iran-abd-ile-anlasma-konusunda-yeni-bir-gelisme-yok-294824)
- 2026-11-03: Al-Araby Al-Jadeed, as relayed by The Moscow Times, reports a temporary deal being prepared through Qatar and Pakistan: nuclear concessions from Iran in exchange for partial release of frozen assets. I could not confirm this independently. [Korrespondent](https://korrespondent.net/world/4925808-ssha-y-yran-hotoviat-vremennoe-myrnoe-sohlashenye)
- 2026-11-02/03: Axios (as cited by other outlets) says Qatar drafted a three-day sequence of confidence-building steps meant to restart **direct** US-Iran talks. A Qatari team met Foreign Minister Araghchi in Tehran on Nov 2, then returned to Doha. [Nation Thailand](https://www.nationthailand.com/news/world/40073049), [Daily Ittehad](https://dailyittehad.com.pk/news/2026/11/03/qatari-mediators-in-tehran-again-as-iran-us-diplomacy-steps-up)
- 2026-11-02: Reuters: Iranian negotiators left Doha on Nov 1 after three days of talks with Qatari mediators. A draft is circulating for feedback and a "follow-up meeting may be held." Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi was in Doha. [Cyprus Mail/Reuters](https://cyprus-mail.com/2026/11/02/iranians-have-left-doha-talks-draft-proposal-for-us-deal-being-circulated-official-says)
- 2026-11-01: Tehran confirms it received a letter from Vice President Vance, which Rezaei says has a different tone. Trump says there will be no strikes before the midterms but has not ruled them out afterward. [Yeshiva World/Reuters](https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/israel-news/2617451/iran-showdown-negotiators-continue-doha-talks-as-tehran-confirms-receiving-letter-from-vice-president-vance.html)
- Late Oct 2026: According to the WSJ, Vance sent the letter to Rezaei at Trump's direction, setting out a framework for negotiations. Trump has played down that it was a negotiation proposal. [UNI India](https://www.uniindia.com/world/us-vance-iran-letter-nuclear-programme/229744)
- 2026-11-02/03: Witkoff's attention is also on Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11. That is working-level, so he may not attend himself. [Asia-Plus](https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/11/03/the-us-russia-and-ukraine-to-hold-new-round-of-talks-in-abu-dhabi-on-november-10-11/)
- 2026-09-22: In New York, Witkoff and Kushner held indirect talks with Araghchi through the Qatari PM. Trump said another round would be "scheduled in the very near future" and predicted a deal right after the midterms. No round followed in October. [France 24](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260922-middle-east-live-yemen-fighting-escalates-as-trump-heads-to-un)
- Late Sep 2026: TASS, citing Axios, says the Qatari mediation effort collapsed and fighting could resume after the midterms. [TASS](https://tass.com/world/2194785)

## 4. Base rates
- Four qualifying in-person rounds in about 8 months of war (Apr 11-12, Jun 21-28, Jul 1-2, Sep 22).
- Using two-month windows from Mar-Apr through Sep-Oct: Mar-Apr, May-Jun, Jul-Aug and Sep-Oct each had at least one meeting.
- Gaps between rounds: about 10 weeks (April to June), 3 days, about 12 weeks (July to September). By Nov 3 the current gap is about 6 weeks. An 8-week window has historically usually caught a round.
- Some rounds fell through: in late June, Witkoff and Kushner went to Doha while Iran refused to meet them at first. [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/us-iran-negotiators-head-doha-meeting-uncertain-rcna352354)

## 5. Other forecasts (prices as of 2026-11-03 18:04 UTC)
- Kalshi, US-Iran senior-level meeting: 29% before Dec 1, 47% before Jan 1. Kalshi's "senior-level" definition may be stricter than this question's.
- Polymarket, next senior diplomatic meeting: 29% by Nov 30, 46.5% by Dec 31.
- Polymarket, where the next meeting takes place: no meeting by Dec 31 at 51.5%, Qatar 16%, Switzerland 5.5%, Saudi Arabia 3%, Oman 1.5%.
- Polymarket, who attends a round of talks by Dec 31: Kushner and Witkoff show 1.00, apparently already resolved by earlier rounds. Vance is at 30.5%.
- Kalshi: China-mediated meeting before Feb 1 at 15%. Nuclear deal before Jan 1 at 10%.
- I found no Metaculus community forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events
- 2026-11-03: US midterms. Reported US strike windows open from Nov 4, and Trump reportedly wants to hit one or two sites, including Pickaxe Mountain. Renewed strikes could shut down meetings or, as after the June strikes, lead to new Doha talks.
- Iran's reply to the Qatari draft and the Vance letter, and a possible follow-up Doha meeting (no date announced).
- Nov 10-11: Abu Dhabi talks on Russia-Ukraine, which compete for Witkoff's time.
- I found no scheduled multilateral venue in November-December that would bring both delegations together.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 8 weeks remain, from Nov 1 to Dec 31, 2026, and resolution comes around Jan 1, 2027. For Yes, at least one authorized US executive-branch negotiator and one authorized Iranian government negotiator must be at the same venue for talks on US-Iran issues. Indirect shuttling through a mediator counts if both sides are at the same venue. Credible sources must report the meeting.

(b) The status quo is No. As of Nov 3, there has been no in-person round since Sep 22. The late-October Doha contacts had Iranians meeting only Qatari mediators. A follow-up meeting has been floated but has no date or venue.

(c) The base rate is high. Since February, every two-month window has contained at least one qualifying round (4 of 4). Gaps between rounds have been about 10 and 12 weeks, and the current gap is already 6 weeks. Taken alone, that suggests roughly 65-70% for an 8-week window. But the war's tempo is now different, with strike threats and stalled mediation, so I discount it.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The Reuters report of Nov 2 says a draft deal is circulating and a "follow-up meeting may be held."
  - Axios (Nov 2-3) reports that Qatar has drafted confidence-building steps meant specifically to restart direct talks.
  - Vance sent a letter to Rezaei in late October that Tehran describes as having a different tone.
  - Trump said in September that he expects a deal right after the midterms.
  - This question's definition is loose: deputy-level negotiators and shuttle formats count.
- **For No:**
  - On Nov 3, Iran said it is "far from agreement" and ties any deal to ending the blockade.
  - Gulf allies were warned of possible US strikes after Nov 4, and Mojtaba Khamenei ordered war preparations.
  - No round happened in October despite Trump's prediction.
  - Witkoff is tied up with Russia-Ukraine talks.
  - Markets put a senior meeting by Dec 31 at about 46-47%.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The US strikes Pickaxe Mountain in mid-November. Iran suspends contact, and mediation stays remote through Qatar until year-end.
- **Yes:** After the midterms, Iran replies to the Qatari draft. Witkoff and Kushner fly to Doha in late November or December for an indirect round with Gharibabadi or Araghchi in the same hotel. This could also happen as a de-escalation round after limited strikes, as happened after the June strikes.

(f) I anchor on the markets at about 47%. Kalshi and Polymarket ask about "senior" meetings, which is probably stricter than this question. Here a deputy-level meeting or a shuttle format at one venue counts, and that is worth a few points upward. The historical base rate also points up. Against that, the strike threats and Iran's hardline statements pull down, and the markets have likely already priced those in. Net, I move slightly above the market, to about 50%.

Probability: 50%

(a) The window runs from Nov 1 to Dec 31, 2026, so about 8 weeks remain, and the result will be known around Jan 1, 2027. For Yes, at least one authorized US negotiator and one authorized Iranian negotiator must be in the same venue, and credible sources must report them holding talks on US-Iran issues. The talks can be indirect, with a mediator shuttling between the two sides.

(b) Status quo: as of Nov 3, no meeting in this window has been reported. Current contacts are indirect, with Iranians meeting Qatari mediators and Washington taking part remotely. If that pattern holds through Dec 31, the answer is No.

(c) Base rate: there have been four qualifying rounds in about 8 months. Every two-month window since the war began contained at least one round, about 4 of 4. Gaps between rounds have run up to about 12 weeks, so an 8-week window starting 6 weeks after the last round is not guaranteed to catch one. A naive base rate is about 65-70%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Nov 2 (Reuters): a draft proposal is circulating and a follow-up meeting "may be held."
- Nov 2-3 (Axios): Qatar has drafted confidence-building steps meant to restart direct talks.
- Nov 1: Vance sent a letter, which Tehran says has a different tone.
- Nov 3: an unconfirmed report of a temporary deal being prepared.
- Precedent: after the June strikes, talks quickly moved to Doha.
- This question's definition is looser than the markets' "senior-level" wording. A Gharibabadi-level meeting with a US envoy in the same venue would count.

Evidence for No:
- Nov 3: a senior Iranian official says the sides are "far from agreement."
- Nov 3: Gulf allies were told to prepare for US strikes after Nov 4, and Khamenei reportedly ordered the armed forces to prepare for war.
- No round took place in October, despite Trump saying on Sep 22 that one would come "in the very near future."
- Witkoff is also committed to the Russia-Ukraine talks.
- Markets price a senior meeting by Dec 31 at about 46-47%.
